PROPOSED FAMILY - no slug emitted; RE-PROPOSED UNCHANGED from the predecessor report, deliberately reusing the same slug because the same prevention addresses both sessions' instances. Warwick asked whether the DB binding was wrong three times. The record shows FIVE occurrences with exactly TWO root causes. Cause A, node_modules does not travel into a git worktree because it is untracked: (1) WO-06, 'I claimed services/asdair/cockpit-api/node_modules/pg existed in your worktree. It does not' - Larry's own words, 'me asserting a state I had not executed, in the same session an audit named that exact habit'; (2) Lane J, three service directories had no node_modules in the worktree so the production path died on Cannot find module 'pg'. Cause B, asdair_rw cannot perform owner-level DDL by design: (3) migration 020's first attempt rolled back with 'permission denied for schema asdair'; (4) WO-05's acceptance criteria were unprovable because no disposable Postgres existed at all; (5) WO-13 AC0 was wrong - asdair_rw cannot CREATE SCHEMA, which applyThrowawaySchema requires, so the DB-gated file fails hard rather than skipping and the order's own zero-skipped figure was unreachable, WRITTEN AFTER Larry had personally hit cause B on migration 020 that same morning. Separately: private_surface pointed at the ROOT of the secrets store in FOUR consecutive orders, and three Keel instances refused on that boundary before the fourth still carried it. Prevention: a resource a worker is bound to is verified by execution at the moment the order is written, or labelled unverified inside the order.

PROPOSED FAMILY - no slug emitted. THE ONE DEFECT IN THIS REPORT THAT WILL RECUR UNCHANGED UNLESS FIXED STRUCTURALLY. Larry bound five concurrently-running lanes to a single disposable Postgres. Consequences, in the map's own words: the cluster reached 98 shops and carried PHOTO 9 / WARWICK 5 / REGULARS 62 rows from sibling lanes, so 'scoping to own-run shop ids is mandatory'; PHOTO rows moved 9 to 17 under Lane J mid-build; the Lane J order had to carry an explicit warning that 'the cluster is shared and moved under Lane G mid-build'. This is a dispatch-architecture defect, not a Work Order defect. The estate already applies isolation to FILES (worktree isolation for concurrent file-mutating subagents) and did not apply it to DATABASES. Prevention: one mutable target per lane, or an explicit shop-id scope declared in the order and enforced by the acceptance query.

TEST SCAFFOLDING CONTAMINATED THE ESTATE TWICE, CONFIRMED, AND THE SECOND WAS THE REPAIR OF THE FIRST. (1) Larry's disposable Postgres held 4 regulars and ZERO rules when Lane J's read-back found it. resolveByCatalogue decides identity against that catalogue, so ~39 read lines against a 4-item catalogue resolves to roughly 4 established and ~35 routed against a frozen 39. Keel's words: 'a reader would see that number and conclude vision collapsed, when the true cause is an unseeded database. That is worse than a wrong number; it is a WRONG NUMBER POINTING AT THE PARKED MECHANISM YOU SPECIFICALLY PROTECTED.' And RULE provenance cannot fire with zero rules, so AC1 and AC2 were jointly unsatisfiable - said rather than bridged. (2) The repair carried the contamination forward: Larry copied the real 109-row catalogue in with 'on conflict (id) do nothing', the four invented fixture rows already occupied ids 3-6, so FOUR REAL PRODUCTS WERE SILENTLY REJECTED and the inventions sat in their place - Lucozade Sport, CRAVENDALE MILK, the real Lenor, and Walkers crisps. Cravendale is precisely the milk the BOB ruling turns on, ruled by Warwick 2026-08-08 and load-bearing in the household knowledge model: Larry's test fixture deleted, from the acceptance target, the single product a standing product ruling is built on. Detection and repair credited: Keel reported near-duplicate identities, Larry checked AT SOURCE rather than at the symptom (live has 109 regulars and 109 distinct normalised names, no duplicates), traced it to his own fixtures, and corrected by overwriting ids 3-6 IN PLACE because delete was blocked by shop_line FKs and in-place update preserves referential integrity. Final state 109 rows, zero fixtures, zero duplicates, and work did not stop for it. THE GENERALISABLE MECHANISM: 'on conflict (id) do nothing' is a silent-loss idiom - it cannot distinguish 'already correct' from 'already wrong' and reports success either way.

A governance change of this weight whose only durable prose lives in a source comment is a documentation defect. Non-blocking; record it at the next map touch.
